part1: accommodation
Do you live in a house or an apartment? What do you like about where you live?
Is there anything you would like to change about it?
neighbours
Do you know your neighbours well? How often do you talk to them?
Do neighbours in your country usually help each other?
clothes
What kind of clothes do you usually wear? Do you wear different clothes on different occasions?
Do you prefer comfortable clothes or fashionable clothes?
birthdays
How do you usually celebrate your birthday? Is it an important day for you?
Did you celebrate your birthday differently when you were a child?
cooking
Do you like cooking? Who usually cooks in your family?
What is the first dish you learned to cook?
mornings
Are you a morning person? What do you usually do in the morning?
Has your morning routine changed in recent years?
handwriting
Do you often write by hand? Do you think handwriting will become less important in the future?
Is your handwriting easy for other people to read?
colours
What is your favourite colour? Do colours affect your mood?
Are there colours that have special meanings in your culture?
parks
Are there many parks in your city? What do people usually do there?
Would you like to have more green spaces near your home?
museums
Do you enjoy visiting museums? Why do some people find museums boring?
What kind of museum would you like to visit in the future?
newspapers
Do you read the news? Where do you usually get your information about what is happening in the world?
Do you trust the news you see on social media?
dreams
Do you often remember your dreams? Do you think dreams have any meaning?
Do you have any dreams about your future career?
planning
Are you someone who plans things carefully or someone who prefers to be spontaneous?
Has being organised ever helped you in your studies or work?
teamwork
Do you prefer working alone or working in a team? Why?
What problems can happen when people work in groups?
patience
Would you say you are a patient person? Can you describe a situation where you had to be patient?
Do you think children today are less patient than in the past?
noise
Is the place where you live noisy? How does noise affect you when you are studying or working?
What could cities do to reduce noise?
cards: sports
Describe a sport or physical activity you enjoy. You should say: what it is · how often you do it · who you do it with · and explain why you enjoy it.
Why do some people not exercise regularly?
Should sport be compulsory in schools?
Do you think professional athletes are paid too much?
reading
Describe a book you have read that you would recommend to others. You should say: what it is about · when you read it · what you liked about it · and explain why you would recommend it.
Do people in your country read as much as they did in the past?
Are electronic books better than paper books?
What can be done to encourage children to read more?
neighbours
Describe a neighbour you know well. You should say: who this person is · how long you have known them · what you do together · and explain what you like about this person.
Why are people today less close to their neighbours than in the past?
Do you think neighbours should help each other more?
What problems can happen between neighbours?
markets
Describe a shop or market you often go to. You should say: where it is · what it sells · how often you go there · and explain why you like going there.
What are the advantages of shopping online compared with going to shops?
Do you think people buy more things than they need?
How can small local shops compete with large supermarkets?
jobs
Describe a job you would like to do in the future. You should say: what the job is · what skills it needs · how you would prepare for it · and explain why you find it attractive.
Is it more important to choose a job you enjoy or a job that pays well?
Why do some people change jobs often?
Which jobs do you think will be most needed in the future?
commuting
Describe a journey you often make. You should say: where you go · how you travel · how long it takes · and explain how you feel about this journey.
How could public transport in your city be improved?
Should cars be banned from city centres?
Do you think self-driving vehicles will become common?
helping
Describe a time when you helped someone. You should say: who you helped · what the problem was · how you helped · and explain how you felt afterwards.
Why do some people volunteer to help others without being paid?
Should schools require students to do community service?
Are people more or less willing to help strangers than in the past?
films
Describe a film you watched recently that you enjoyed. You should say: what it was about · where and when you watched it · who you watched it with · and explain why you enjoyed it.
Is it better to watch films at the cinema or at home?
Do you think violent films have a bad effect on young people?
Should governments give money to support the film industry?
time-management
Describe a time when you were very busy. You should say: when it was · what you had to do · how you managed your time · and explain how you felt about it.
Why do some people find it hard to manage their time?
Is being on time as important as it used to be?
How can employers help people avoid too much work stress?
communication

Describe a time when you had difficulty communicating with someone. You should say: who the person was · what the situation was · why it was difficult · and explain what you learned from the experience.
Why do misunderstandings happen so often between people?
Is communication easier today because of technology?
How important are non-verbal signals such as body language?

skills: Why do some people find it easier to learn new skills than others?
Which skills should schools teach that they do not teach now?
Do you think people will need to keep learning new skills throughout their working lives? Why?
travel: Why do so many people enjoy travelling to other countries?
How has travelling changed compared with the past?
Is it better to travel alone or with other people?
people: What qualities make a person admirable in your culture?
Do you think celebrities are good role models for young people?
How do the people we admire change as we grow older?
media: How do people in your country usually get their news?
Do you think the media has too much influence on what people think?
Is it a problem that some people only read news that agrees with their own views?
decisions: Should parents make important decisions for their children?
Do people make better decisions alone or in groups?
Is it always better to take time before making a big decision?
technology: What are the disadvantages of relying too much on technology?
How do older people cope with new technology?
Do you think robots will replace many jobs in the future?
celebrations: How do people in your country usually celebrate important events?
Are celebrations today less traditional than they were in the past?
Should governments spend public money on celebrations?
places: What makes a place a good place to relax?
Do people need to live near nature to be happy?
How are public places in cities changing?
memories: Why do some memories stay with us longer than others?
Is it important to keep things like photos and letters to remember the past?
Do you think people today record too much of their lives online?
goals: Why do some people set goals while others do not?
Is it better to have one big goal or several small goals?
How can society help young people achieve their goals?
gifts: Why do people give gifts on special occasions?
Is it better to give money or a present?
Do you think people spend too much on gifts nowadays?
food: How have eating habits in your country changed in recent years?
Why do some people prefer fast food to home cooking?
Should governments do more to encourage healthy eating?
apps: Why do people download so many apps?
Do apps make life easier or more stressful?
Should children be allowed to use apps without parental control?
weather: How does the weather affect people's mood and behaviour?
Do you think climate change will change the way people live?
Should schools and employers change their schedules during extreme weather?
teachers: Do you think teachers are respected enough in your country?
Will technology ever replace teachers in classrooms?
history: Why is it important to preserve historic buildings?
Should history be a compulsory subject at school?
Is it better to learn history from books or by visiting historical places?
photos: Why do people like taking photos?
Has photography become more or less meaningful since smartphones appeared?
Is it acceptable to post photos of other people online without asking them?
advice: Who do people usually ask for advice, and why?
Is advice from older people always useful for younger people?
Is it better to follow advice or to learn from your own mistakes?
daily-life: How have people's daily routines changed over the last few decades?
Do you think people today have enough free time?
Would a shorter working week improve people's lives?
possessions: Why do some people like to own expensive things?
Do you think people are too materialistic nowadays?
Is it better to buy new things or to repair old ones?
traditions: Why is it important for a country to keep its traditions?
Do young people care about traditions as much as older people?
How can traditions be passed on to the next generation?
nature: Why do many people enjoy spending time in nature?
Should the government limit tourist numbers in natural areas?
What can individuals do to protect the natural environment?
music: How does music influence people's emotions?
Do you think a person's taste in music depends on their age?
Should schools spend more time teaching music?
promises: Why do people sometimes break promises?
Is it ever acceptable to break a promise?
How important is trust in a friendship or at work?
changes: Why do some people find change difficult?
Is change usually good for society?
How can people prepare for big changes in their lives?
